opening.argument: The video is plainly an educational medical explanation: it identifies “Myths and Facts of Radiation Therapy” and examines common beliefs about the treatment. The speaker explains that radiation may be used to suppress pain in certain circumstances, then directly addresses the myth that the technique is painful, stating that no pain occurs during its application. The doctor-led discussion presents medical information about treatment effects and side effects, with hospital branding and contact details serving as institutional context. Nothing offers an investment, payment, credential, or participation opportunity.

citations.quote: Myths and Facts of Radiation Therapy | Dr. Kanika Sharma Sood (Hindi)
So, today we want to know about some of the myths and illusions that many people have been rumored.
Now a myth is that the technique is very painful. This is not true that the technique is very painful. During the application of radiation we get no pain.
